SIGR50MKplPxkwHqzYpK_w.zh: 疫情更新:  今年第 11 週(3/16-22)全球陽性率上升為 2.47%,其中東南亞區署、東地中海區署陽性率明顯增加。 德國疫情呈下降,目前處低點,第 13 週新增 282 例病例;變異株以 NB.1.8.1(68%)為主,另變異株 BA.3.2 占比上升,從今年9-10 週的 5%,上升至第 10-11 週的 11%。 英國疫情略升,第 13 週實驗室檢測陽性率略增至 2.1%。變異株以 XFG 占大宗,BA.3 於 2/16-3/1 占比為 2.13%。 GISAID 去年 12 月迄今的病毒株定序資料顯示,BA.3.2 多數易感宿主為年輕族群,其中,愛爾蘭高達 38.8%及法國 27%病例為 18 歲以下族群;美國 49.1%及盧森堡 23.4%病例為 10 歲以下族群,與其他變異株感染病患的年齡層分布顯著不同。  評估與建議:  近期全球流行變異株以 XFG 占比最高(占 31.44%),其次為NB.1.8.1(30.68%),BA.3.2 占比上升至 12.5%。WHO 公布之 COVID-19 全球長期快速風險評估(第 9 版),評估對全球公共衛生的整體風險屬中等。鑒於自然感染與疫苗帶來的群體免疫力提升,以及臨床治療的進步,全球住院與死亡數自 2022 年以來明顯下降。 目前多數流行變異株為 Omicron JN.1 及其衍生亞型,雖具備免疫逃脫能力,惟不至於造成疾病嚴重度增加,然有 6%的有症狀病例出現長新冠症狀;現階段 COVID-19 尚未形成穩定季節性流行規律,多數國家已減少常規檢測通報,汙水與定醫監測成為重要的補充監測方式。 WHO 指出,目前疫苗仍能有效預防重症與死亡,並建議優先保護高風險族群、與流感疫苗共同施打;同時透過《冠狀病毒疾病威脅管理策略計劃》呼籲各國整合防治計畫,持續加強監測、保護高風險族群、維持醫療與公衛韌性,並落實風險溝通。
SIGR50MKplPxkwHqzYpK_w.en: Epidemic update: In week 11 of this year (16–22 March), the global positivity rate rose to 2.47%, with notable increases in the WHO South-East Asia and Eastern Mediterranean regions. Germany's epidemic is declining and is currently at a low point, with 282 new cases reported in week 13. NB.1.8.1 (68%) remains the predominant variant, while the share of BA.3.2 has risen from 5% in weeks 9–10 of this year to 11% in weeks 10–11. The UK's epidemic has risen slightly, and laboratory test positivity increased slightly to 2.1% in week 13. XFG accounts for the largest share of variants, and BA.3 accounted for 2.13% during 16 February–1 March. Sequencing data in GISAID since December last year show that most BA.3.2 infections occur in young people: 38.8% of cases in the Republic of Ireland and 27% in France were under 18 years, and 49.1% of cases in the United States and 23.4% in Luxembourg were under 10 years, a significantly different age distribution from patients infected with other variants. Assessment and recommendations: XFG currently accounts for the highest share of circulating variants globally (31.44%), followed by NB.1.8.1 (30.68%), and BA.3.2 has risen to 12.5%. WHO's global long-term rapid risk assessment for COVID-19 (9th edition) rates the overall risk to global public health as moderate. Given population immunity from natural infection and vaccination, and advances in clinical treatment, global hospitalizations and deaths have declined markedly since 2022. Most circulating variants are Omicron JN.1 and its descendant subtypes; although they have immune escape capacity, they do not cause greater disease severity, but 6% of symptomatic cases develop long COVID symptoms. COVID-19 has not yet established a stable seasonal pattern, and most countries have reduced routine testing and reporting, so wastewater and sentinel physician surveillance have become important supplementary methods. WHO notes that current vaccines remain effective at preventing severe disease and death, and recommends prioritizing high-risk groups and co-administration with influenza vaccines. Through its Strategic Plan for Coronavirus Disease Threat Management, WHO calls on countries to integrate prevention and control plans, continue strengthening surveillance, protect high-risk groups, maintain health system and public health resilience, and implement risk communication.
